settings.heading: What you are dealing with
settings.intro: A setup is the start. These are the problems that show up in the months after it.
items: A setup that works today drifts. Nobody updates it, and it slowly stops matching how you work.
Tools change every month. You cannot tell which changes matter and which do not.
New tasks keep arriving. Your setup covers last quarter's work, not this quarter's.
Your team does not use what was built. It sits there while people work the old way.
You hit a problem and have nobody to ask. Nobody else understands your setup.
The quality of the output varies. Some days it is good and some days it is not, and you do not know why.
Under pressure, you go back to old habits. A setup only helps if it is used in the busiest weeks.
Every new tool needs judging. Security, cost and fit, and you have no time to check each one.
Confidentiality rules go out of date. Tools change their terms and features, and your rules do not follow.
You want your assistant involved and have no plan. Who does what, and in which order?
Improvements wait for an owner. Everyone agrees something should be better, and nobody has the time.
You cannot tell whether it saves you time. It feels useful, but nobody has measured it since the first week.
